papers.title: The herd immunity attractor: selection, drift, and the steady-state undersupply of vaccination in 195 countries, 1980–2025
papers.abstract: Introduction Vaccination is the canonical positive externality in health economics: because each vaccination protects others, decentralized choice is predicted to stall below the herd immunity threshold. Yet little evidence exists on the law of motion that governs national coverage. This study estimates it directly. Methods I model the vaccinate-or-not decision of a heterogeneous household population as an expected-utility problem whose net payoff declines in the vaccinated share, aggregate it through an explicit revision protocol into a selection-mutation (replicator-mutator) equation in which payoff-responsive switching coexists with health-system contact and attrition hazards, and estimate the resulting equation on the World Health Organization/United Nations Children's Fund (WHO/UNICEF) Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC, 2025 revision) for 195 countries over 1980-2025, with UN cohort denominators and World Bank income and health-system capacity controls. An exact identification result shows that the linear turnover coefficient equals the difference between the law of motion at full and at zero coverage, so it is identified from boundary observations independently of the payoff parameters, whereas the payoff slope is identified only where coverage traverses the simplex. Results First, in the interior of the coverage range, the dynamics are dominated by a strong linear restoring force, implying an annual turnover of 15%–25% of the relevant pool; the payoff slope is statistically weak there, and interior data cannot distinguish institutional flows from payoff-insensitive revision, so the estimated hazards bound the institutional component from above. Second, the free-riding signature appears where it is identified: sharply in the Hib rollout, which spans the full coverage range, and weakly on the first-dose DTP margin. Third, every country's law of motion has a stable interior rest point; the births-weighted world rest point for first-dose measles vaccination is 78%, below the 92%–94% herd band; 74% of countries rest below it, and a coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) era shift lowered the median rest point by 3.3 points. Discussion Because the leverage of retention over payoff instruments equals 1/(1 − x * ) under the replicator protocol and diverges along the last mile under any smooth, bounded choice protocol, closing the gap is a default-and-retention problem rather than a price problem.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the dynamics of vaccination coverage across 195 countries from 1980 to 2025, focusing on the herd immunity threshold and the factors influencing vaccination decisions. It models the vaccinate-or-not decision as an expected-utility problem, incorporating health-system contact and attrition hazards. The results show a strong linear restoring force in the interior of the coverage range, with an annual turnover of 15%–25%. The study also identifies a free-riding signature in the Hib rollout and on the first-dose DTP margin. The findings suggest that closing the vaccination gap is a default-and-retention problem rather than a price problem. The analysis highlights that the world rest point for first-dose measles vaccination is 78%, below the herd band, with a significant shift due to the COVID-19 era. The study's evidence is based on WHO/UNICEF data and includes controls for income and health-system capacity, but the limitations are not explicitly detailed in the supplied evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 疫苗接种 是卫生经济学中典型的正外部性:因为每个 疫苗接种 都保护其他人,所以预计去中心化选择将停滞在群体免疫阈值以下。提供的证据并未报告该研究解决的具体科学或公共卫生问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究直接估计了影响国家 疫苗接种 覆盖范围的运动定律。所提供的证据并未报告具体的研究设计、人群或环境。
elements_zh.methods: 我将异质家庭人口的接种或不接种决策建模为预期效用问题,其净收益随着疫苗接种份额的增加而下降,通过明确的修订方案将其汇总为选择 突变(复制子 - 变异子)方程,其中收益响应切换与卫生系统接触和损耗风险共存,并根据世界卫生组织/联合国儿童基金会(WHO/UNICEF)估计所得方程1980-2025 年 195 个国家的国家免疫覆盖率估计(WUENIC,2025 年修订版),采用联合国 队列研究 分母和世界银行收入和卫生系统能力控制。

papers.title_zh: 群体免疫吸引子:1980-2025 年 195 个国家 疫苗接种 的选择、漂移和稳态供应不足
papers.source_body_en: Introduction Vaccination is the canonical positive externality in health economics: because each vaccination protects others, decentralized choice is predicted to stall below the herd immunity threshold. Yet little evidence exists on the law of motion that governs national coverage. This study estimates it directly. Methods I model the vaccinate-or-not decision of a heterogeneous household population as an expected-utility problem whose net payoff declines in the vaccinated share, aggregate it through an explicit revision protocol into a selection-mutation (replicator-mutator) equation in which payoff-responsive switching coexists with health-system contact and attrition hazards, and estimate the resulting equation on the World Health Organization/United Nations Children's Fund (WHO/UNICEF) Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC, 2025 revision) for 195 countries over 1980-2025, with UN cohort denominators and World Bank income and health-system capacity controls. An exact identification result shows that the linear turnover coefficient equals the difference between the law of motion at full and at zero coverage, so it is identified from boundary observations independently of the payoff parameters, whereas the payoff slope is identified only where coverage traverses the simplex. Results First, in the interior of the coverage range, the dynamics are dominated by a strong linear restoring force, implying an annual turnover of 15%–25% of the relevant pool; the payoff slope is statistically weak there, and interior data cannot distinguish institutional flows from payoff-insensitive revision, so the estimated hazards bound the institutional component from above. Second, the free-riding signature appears where it is identified: sharply in the Hib rollout, which spans the full coverage range, and weakly on the first-dose DTP margin. Third, every country's law of motion has a stable interior rest point; the births-weighted world rest point for first-dose measles vaccination is 78%, below the 92%–94% herd band; 74% of countries rest below it, and a coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) era shift lowered the median rest point by 3.3 points. Discussion Because the leverage of retention over payoff instruments equals 1/(1 − x * ) under the replicator protocol and diverges along the last mile under any smooth, bounded choice protocol, closing the gap is a default-and-retention problem rather than a price problem.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介 疫苗接种 是卫生经济学中典型的正外部性:因为每个 疫苗接种 都保护其他人,所以预计去中心化选择将停滞在群体免疫阈值以下。然而,关于支配全国范围的运动定律的证据却很少。这项研究直接估计了它。方法我将异质家庭人口的接种或不接种决策建模为预期效用问题,其净收益随着疫苗接种份额的下降而下降,通过明确的修订方案将其汇总为选择突变(复制子-变异子)方程,其中收益响应切换与卫生系统接触和损耗风险共存,并根据世界卫生组织/联合国儿童基金会(WHO/UNICEF)估计所得方程1980-2025 年 195 个国家的国家免疫覆盖率估计(WUENIC,2025 年修订版),采用联合国 队列研究 分母和世界银行收入和卫生系统能力控制。精确的识别结果表明,线性周转系数等于完全覆盖和零覆盖时运动定律之间的差,因此它是根据与支付参数无关的边界观察来识别的,而支付斜率仅在覆盖穿过单纯形的地方被识别。结果首先,在覆盖范围内部,动态以强线性恢复力为主,这意味着相关池的年周转率为15%–25%;那里的收益斜率在统计上很弱,并且内部数据无法区分制度流动和对收益不敏感的修正,因此估计的风险从上面限制了制度成分。其次,搭便车特征出现在它被识别的地方:在跨越整个覆盖范围的 Hib 推出中急剧变化,而在第一剂 DTP 裕度上较弱。第三,每个国家的运动规律都有一个稳定的内部休息点;第一剂 麻疹 疫苗接种 的出生加权世界休息点为 78%,低于 92%–94% 群体范围;74% 的国家/地区休息点低于该水平,2019 年冠状病毒病 (COVID-19) 时代的转变使休息点中位数降低了 3.3 个百分点。讨论 由于在复制协议下,留存相对于支付工具的杠杆等于 1/(1 − x * ),而在任何平滑、有界选择协议下,在最后一英里上会出现分歧,因此缩小差距是违约和留存问题,而不是价格问题。

papers.title: Public Health Pharmacology: a framework for population-level immunologic monitoring (PLIM) to optimize vaccine performance in Africa

source_records.title: Public Health Pharmacology: a framework for population-level immunologic monitoring (PLIM) to optimize vaccine performance in Africa

papers.priority_tier_reason: 补充性记录、预印本或证据完整度有限
papers.full_text: Despite high administrative immunization coverage across Sub-Saharan Africa, unexpected infectious disease outbreaks pose significant public health challenges. Traditional tracking relies heavily on logistical inputs and reactive surveillance, leaving an unmonitored biological gap in real-world host immunity. This paper presents a novel systems-design conceptual framework for Population-Level Immunologic Monitoring (PLIM) as a core operational tool of Public Health Pharmacology (PHP) to systematically bridge this gap. PLIM operates across three interconnected pillars: (1) biological sentinel surveillance using field-stabilized samples, (2) risk stratification mapping the climatic-biological nexus, and (3) near-real-time policy feedback via digital health infrastructure. To demonstrate operational plausibility, we describe a prospective “Pathfinder Pilot” validation roadmap in Rwanda. This theoretical proof-of-concept model details a logistics blueprint utilizing Dried Blood Spot (DBS) sampling paired with quantitative ELISAs and T-cell Activation Assays (TASA) integrated into existing DHIS2 software to monitor population cohorts against the Population Immunologic Threshold (PIT)—a composite metric linking individual correlates of protection to herd immunity thresholds. Crucially, PLIM complements existing administrative tracking, pharmacovigilance, and epidemiological outbreak investigations. By isolating biological host factors, the framework provides an intermediate biological audit layer. This empowers public health managers to detect waning immunity and map “biological cold spots” before outbreaks occur, advancing immunologic equity across resource-limited settings. MethodsThe PLIM framework: a systems approach to vaccine pharmacodynamicsThe Population-Level Immunologic Monitoring (PLIM) framework is designed to function as a diagnostic engine of Public Health Pharmacology. Unlike traditional pharmacovigilance, which relies on passive safety reporting or sporadic efficacy studies, PLIM actively and systematically seeks to verify the biological performance of vaccines in real-world populations. The framework operates through three interconnected pillars: (1) Sentinel Surveillance, (2) Risk Stratification, and (3) Real-Time Policy Feedback.Methodological boundaries: immunogenicity, protection, effectiveness, and impactTo ensure conceptual clarity within the Public Health Pharmacology paradigm, the operational parameters of PLIM would have to be explicitly distinguished from standard epidemiological and clinical trial metrics. In this respect, the following terminologies are clarified.Immunogenicity refers strictly to the intrinsic capacity of a vaccine to elicit a measurable immune response (such as neutralizing antibody titers or antigen-specific T-cell activation) in an individual host environment under controlled settings.Protection represents the physiological state resulting from that immune response, defining whether an individual has achieved a threshold of immunity sufficient to resist clinical infection or severe pathogenesis.Population immunologic threshold: While classic vaccinology focuses on an individual Correlate of Protection (CoP)- defined by Plotkin (10) as a specific immune marker statistically associated with protection from clinical disease- Public Health Pharmacology requires a macroscopic, population-level surrogate. We define the Population Immunologic Threshold (PIT) as the critical proportion of a population that must sustain individual immune responses above the validated protective threshold to interrupt community transmission. For pathogens with established humoral correlates (such as measles, rubella, or tetanus toxoid), PIT is mathematically anchored to herd immunity dynamics ( PIT=1−1/R0VE ), where R0 is the basic reproduction number and VE is field vaccine effectiveness). For example, measles requires a PIT where ≥93−−95% of individuals maintain neutralizing antibody titers ≥120mIU/mL . However, for complex pathogens lacking a single, binary antibody cut-off (such as malaria or tuberculosis), PIT cannot be treated as an absolute biological guarantee. In such contexts, PLIM utilizes PIT as an empirical, risk-stratified benchmark that combines quantitative antibody concentrations with cellular activation markers (e.g., TASA) to grade relative population vulnerability rather than predict binary sterile protection.Vaccine effectiveness evaluates how well a vaccine prevents specific clinical endpoints within a dynamic, real-world population, factoring in logistics, cold chain compliance, and field execution.Public health impact measures the downstream macro-level societal benefits, such as reductions in crude mortality, changes in transmission dynamics, or the preservation of healthcare capacity.Operational distinction from conventional surveillancePLIM occupies a distinct diagnostic niche across the public health continuum:Routine epidemiological disease surveillance: Operates downstream and reactively, registering clinical disease incidence, syndromic presentations, and outbreak clusters. It signals a failure after transmission has already propagated.Conventional vaccine effectiveness studies: Typically utilize observational designs (such as test-negative case–control studies) to calculate real-world protection against symptomatic disease endpoints post-licensure. While essential, VE studies are retrospective and resource-intensive, often evaluating outcomes months or years after programmatic delivery.Serosurveillance/sero-epidemiology: Predominantly relies on periodic, cross-sectional population surveys measuring cumulative seroprevalence. Its primary utility is charting past natural exposure or macro-level disease penetration.In contrast, PLIM functions as an active, prospective pharmacodynamic audit. By continuously measuring quantitative immunogenic yield (titers and cellular kinetics) in sentinel cohorts post-vaccination, PLIM isolates the intermediate biological variable between administrative coverage (logistics) and clinical disease (epidemiology). This proactive posture enables health systems to detect waning antibody kinetics and map “biological cold spots” months before clinical breakthrough infections occur.The PLIM programme focuses its analytical lens strictly on the first two variables; aggregating individual immunogenicity data into population-level trends to map verified physiological protection (Figure 1). It does not replace field-level vaccine effectiveness designs or epidemiological outbreak tracking; rather, it provides the missing biological baseline that explains why a vaccine succeeds or fails to achieve its intended public health impact.Figure 1The public health pharmacology cycle of immunologic monitoring (PLIM). A closed-loop system where sentinel immunologic data (Input) is filtered through population risk factors (Analysis) to trigger specific programmatic adjustments (Output). The cycle proceeds in four stages: (A) Sentinel Input utilizes feasible sampling methods like Dried Blood Spots (DBS) from representative district cohorts; (B) The Pharmacological Filter stratifies this data against biological risks such as genetic polymorphisms (HLA), environmental interference (NTM), and co-infections; (C) Programmatic Output generates actionable intelligence (e.g., booster campaigns or formulation updates); and (D) System Integration feeds these insights back into the National Immunization Program to optimize future delivery.Infographic illustrating a cyclical immunization program workflow with four labeled sections: (A) Sentinel Input collects dried blood spots from district cohorts; (B) Pharmacological Filter analyzes genetic, environmental, and co-infection factors; (C) Programmatic Output delivers targeted interventions like booster campaigns, formulation updates, and cold-chain rectification; (D) System Integration feeds insights back into the National Immunization Program to optimize delivery and protection.Pillar 1: sentinel immunogenicity surveillanceTo minimize the logistical burden on resource-limited health systems, PLIM moves away from universal testing. Instead, it utilizes a sentinel surveillance model, adapting strategies successfully employed in HIV and malaria monitoring, as shown in Figure 2.Figure 2The sentinel immunogenicity surveillance infrastructure and the climatic-biological nexus. Schematic representation of the PLIM Pillar 1 and 2 architecture. (A) Decentralized sample collection using dried blood spots (DBS) at the district level, integrated into routine vaccination points. (B) The central laboratory analysis phase, highlighting the transition from standard serology to field-adapted T-cell assays (e.g., TASA). (C) The Climatic-Biological Nexus, illustrating how external stressors such as extreme heat, thermal instability, and nutritional shifts, act as biological modifiers that trigger systemic inflammation and compromise vaccine-induced memory cell formation.Infographic illustrating decentralized blood sample collection from rural clinics using dried blood spot cards, shipment without cold chain to national labs for antibody and T-cell assays, and analysis. Also depicts how extreme heat, nutritional deficiency, and parasitic load stressors impact biological systems, affecting inflammation, cortisol levels, and vaccine memory cell formation, thereby influencing laboratory immunogenicity results.District level (sample collection and surveillance architecture)To achieve representative surveillance without overburdening primary health systems, sentinel site selection follows a stratified purposive sampling design across three primary ecological and health-system strata comprising high-density urban settings characterized by high population turnover, variable informal settlement coverage, and elevated transmission velocity; rural endemic regions burdened by high prevalences of parasitic co-infections such as malaria and schistosomiasis alongside documented nutritional vulnerabilities; and agro-climatic thermal stress zones encompassing peripheral districts subject to documented ambient heat extremes and extended last-mile cold-chain transit lines. Within each sentinel facility, representative sampling is linked directly to routine public health touchpoints, focusing primarily on infants presenting for routine Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) schedules, including the 9-month Measles-Rubella 1 (MR1) and 15–18 month MR2 milestones, supplemented by pregnant women during routine antenatal care visits. Sampling operates on a dual cadence that combines rapid, rolling cross-sectional bi-annual audits- such as testing 50 consecutive infants per sentinel facility twice yearly- to track macro-level community seroprotection rates against seasonal climatic and nutritional variations, alongside prospective longitudinal cohort tracking utilizing nested cohorts monitored at defined post-vaccination intervals encompassing a Day 0 baseline, 28–35 days post-immunization for peak seroconversion assessment, and 6–9 months post-immunization to determine early antibody decay kinetics. Sample stabilization relies entirely on Dried Blood Spots (DBS), which are validated as a thermostable, cost-effective serosurveillance modality in remote settings that completely circumvents cold-chain transport requirements (11, 12).National reference level (analysis)Samples are transported to central reference laboratories for analysis. This includes quantitative ELISAs for antibody titers and, where infrastructure permits, field-adapted T-cell assays (such as simplified ELISpot) to measure cellular immunity. Cellular markers are critical, as they often correlate better with long-term protection than antibodies alone, particularly for complex pathogens like malaria and tuberculosis (13). Recent technological advancements now allow for robust, antigen-specific T-cell monitoring using capillary fingerprick samples, effectively bridging the gap between sophisticated laboratory immunology and field-level practicality (14).IntegrationThese immunologic data points are not siloed but are integrated directly into national health information systems, such as the DHIS2 Tracker. This integration creates a “live map” of population immunity, allowing program managers to visualize protection levels alongside standard coverage rates (15). Recent data synthesis reports from the Rwanda Ministry of Health confirm that the existing digital health ecosystem demonstrates high data consistency and “plausibility” for routine immunization metrics, providing a validated foundation for this immunologic integration (16).Furthermore, emerging environmental health paradigms suggest that the vaccine performance gap in vulnerable settings may be influenced by the Climatic-Biological Nexus. Environmental shifts, spanning ambient heat extremes to seasonal nutritional fluctuations, represent external stressors that could plausibly modulate host physiology alongside well-documented cold-chain transit vulnerabilities (17, 18). Preliminary physiological evidence indicates that prolonged exposure to high ambient temperatures is associated with systemic inflammatory responses and altered neuroendocrine signaling, raising the biologically plausible hypothesis that chronic thermal stress may influence adaptive immune kinetics, including cellular activation and antibody longevity (17). full_text_sections.abstract: Despite high administrative immunization coverage across Sub-Saharan Africa, unexpected infectious disease outbreaks pose significant public health challenges. Traditional tracking relies heavily on logistical inputs and reactive surveillance, leaving an unmonitored biological gap in real-world host immunity. This paper presents a novel systems-design conceptual framework for Population-Level Immunologic Monitoring (PLIM) as a core operational tool of Public Health Pharmacology (PHP) to systematically bridge this gap. PLIM operates across three interconnected pillars: (1) biological sentinel surveillance using field-stabilized samples, (2) risk stratification mapping the climatic-biological nexus, and (3) near-real-time policy feedback via digital health infrastructure. To demonstrate operational plausibility, we describe a prospective “Pathfinder Pilot” validation roadmap in Rwanda. This theoretical proof-of-concept model details a logistics blueprint utilizing Dried Blood Spot (DBS) sampling paired with quantitative ELISAs and T-cell Activation Assays (TASA) integrated into existing DHIS2 software to monitor population cohorts against the Population Immunologic Threshold (PIT)—a composite metric linking individual correlates of protection to herd immunity thresholds. Crucially, PLIM complements existing administrative tracking, pharmacovigilance, and epidemiological outbreak investigations. By isolating biological host factors, the framework provides an intermediate biological audit layer. This empowers public health managers to detect waning immunity and map “biological cold spots” before outbreaks occur, advancing immunologic equity across resource-limited settings.
full_text_sections.methods: MethodsThe PLIM framework: a systems approach to vaccine pharmacodynamicsThe Population-Level Immunologic Monitoring (PLIM) framework is designed to function as a diagnostic engine of Public Health Pharmacology. Unlike traditional pharmacovigilance, which relies on passive safety reporting or sporadic efficacy studies, PLIM actively and systematically seeks to verify the biological performance of vaccines in real-world populations. The framework operates through three interconnected pillars: (1) Sentinel Surveillance, (2) Risk Stratification, and (3) Real-Time Policy Feedback.Methodological boundaries: immunogenicity, protection, effectiveness, and impactTo ensure conceptual clarity within the Public Health Pharmacology paradigm, the operational parameters of PLIM would have to be explicitly distinguished from standard epidemiological and clinical trial metrics. In this respect, the following terminologies are clarified.Immunogenicity refers strictly to the intrinsic capacity of a vaccine to elicit a measurable immune response (such as neutralizing antibody titers or antigen-specific T-cell activation) in an individual host environment under controlled settings.Protection represents the physiological state resulting from that immune response, defining whether an individual has achieved a threshold of immunity sufficient to resist clinical infection or severe pathogenesis.Population immunologic threshold: While classic vaccinology focuses on an individual Correlate of Protection (CoP)- defined by Plotkin (10) as a specific immune marker statistically associated with protection from clinical disease- Public Health Pharmacology requires a macroscopic, population-level surrogate. We define the Population Immunologic Threshold (PIT) as the critical proportion of a population that must sustain individual immune responses above the validated protective threshold to interrupt community transmission. For pathogens with established humoral correlates (such as measles, rubella, or tetanus toxoid), PIT is mathematically anchored to herd immunity dynamics ( PIT=1−1/R0VE ), where R0 is the basic reproduction number and VE is field vaccine effectiveness). For example, measles requires a PIT where ≥93−−95% of individuals maintain neutralizing antibody titers ≥120mIU/mL . However, for complex pathogens lacking a single, binary antibody cut-off (such as malaria or tuberculosis), PIT cannot be treated as an absolute biological guarantee. In such contexts, PLIM utilizes PIT as an empirical, risk-stratified benchmark that combines quantitative antibody concentrations with cellular activation markers (e.g., TASA) to grade relative population vulnerability rather than predict binary sterile protection.Vaccine effectiveness evaluates how well a vaccine prevents specific clinical endpoints within a dynamic, real-world population, factoring in logistics, cold chain compliance, and field execution.Public health impact measures the downstream macro-level societal benefits, such as reductions in crude mortality, changes in transmission dynamics, or the preservation of healthcare capacity.Operational distinction from conventional surveillancePLIM occupies a distinct diagnostic niche across the public health continuum:Routine epidemiological disease surveillance: Operates downstream and reactively, registering clinical disease incidence, syndromic presentations, and outbreak clusters. It signals a failure after transmission has already propagated.Conventional vaccine effectiveness studies: Typically utilize observational designs (such as test-negative case–control studies) to calculate real-world protection against symptomatic disease endpoints post-licensure. While essential, VE studies are retrospective and resource-intensive, often evaluating outcomes months or years after programmatic delivery.Serosurveillance/sero-epidemiology: Predominantly relies on periodic, cross-sectional population surveys measuring cumulative seroprevalence. Its primary utility is charting past natural exposure or macro-level disease penetration.In contrast, PLIM functions as an active, prospective pharmacodynamic audit. By continuously measuring quantitative immunogenic yield (titers and cellular kinetics) in sentinel cohorts post-vaccination, PLIM isolates the intermediate biological variable between administrative coverage (logistics) and clinical disease (epidemiology). This proactive posture enables health systems to detect waning antibody kinetics and map “biological cold spots” months before clinical breakthrough infections occur.The PLIM programme focuses its analytical lens strictly on the first two variables; aggregating individual immunogenicity data into population-level trends to map verified physiological protection (Figure 1). It does not replace field-level vaccine effectiveness designs or epidemiological outbreak tracking; rather, it provides the missing biological baseline that explains why a vaccine succeeds or fails to achieve its intended public health impact.Figure 1The public health pharmacology cycle of immunologic monitoring (PLIM). A closed-loop system where sentinel immunologic data (Input) is filtered through population risk factors (Analysis) to trigger specific programmatic adjustments (Output). The cycle proceeds in four stages: (A) Sentinel Input utilizes feasible sampling methods like Dried Blood Spots (DBS) from representative district cohorts; (B) The Pharmacological Filter stratifies this data against biological risks such as genetic polymorphisms (HLA), environmental interference (NTM), and co-infections; (C) Programmatic Output generates actionable intelligence (e.g., booster campaigns or formulation updates); and (D) System Integration feeds these insights back into the National Immunization Program to optimize future delivery.Infographic illustrating a cyclical immunization program workflow with four labeled sections: (A) Sentinel Input collects dried blood spots from district cohorts; (B) Pharmacological Filter analyzes genetic, environmental, and co-infection factors; (C) Programmatic Output delivers targeted interventions like booster campaigns, formulation updates, and cold-chain rectification; (D) System Integration feeds insights back into the National Immunization Program to optimize delivery and protection.Pillar 1: sentinel immunogenicity surveillanceTo minimize the logistical burden on resource-limited health systems, PLIM moves away from universal testing. full_text_sections.discussion: DiscussionToward an era of verified protectionThe transition from a global health “access era” to one of “verified protection” requires a fundamental recalibration of our evaluative tools. As immunization systems across Africa evolve from basic delivery models toward precision public health, there is an urgent need to move beyond administrative coverage as the primary surrogate for success.The PLIM framework addresses this need by operationalizing Public Health Pharmacology (PHP), providing the empirical engine required to move the discipline from theoretical definition to field-level application. Traditional pharmacology often terminates its inquiry at the conclusion of a clinical trial, assuming that “efficacy” under ideal conditions translates linearly to “effectiveness” in the real world. However, as established in the foundational work of this field, Public Health Pharmacology posits that the interaction between a biological agent and a population is inherently dynamic, shaped by a complex interplay of host genomics, environmental stressors, and climatic volatility (9).In this context, PLIM serves as the “pharmacodynamic monitor” for the last mile. While implementation science focuses on whether the vaccine reached the child, PHP asks the deeper pharmacological question: Did the vaccine induce the intended biological mechanism within this specific host environment? This distinction is critical for pathogens like malaria and tuberculosis, where environmental mycobacterial interference and parasitic co-infections significantly alter the pharmacological yield of the intervention (1, 22). By routinely measuring these immune outputs, health systems can finally bridge the gap between laboratory science and field-level implementation.This shift in focus from “doses” to “protection” carries profound ethical implications for health equity. Current metrics, while logistically useful, can inadvertently mask systemic vulnerabilities. A district may report 95% administrative coverage yet harbor significant “biological cold spots”- pockets of the population where protection may be diminished, potentially associated with climate-driven cold-chain failures or nutritional variances. By relying solely on coverage, we render these unprotected populations invisible. PLIM offers a data-driven pathway to Immunologic Equity, ensuring that high-risk communities are not only reached but effectively protected. Identifying a community where vaccine take is hindered by a high helminth burden, for instance, allows for targeted adjunct interventions—such as integrated deworming and vaccination—rather than the redundant administration of ineffective doses. This strategy ensures that resource allocation is dictated by biological need and verified outcome rather than administrative targets (8).While PLIM champions the objective auditing of biological outcomes, significant caution is warranted when interpreting humoral titers or cellular markers as direct proof of clinical protection. Biological correlates of protection are inherently probabilistic rather than deterministic. Elevated serum IgG concentrations or detectable antigen-specific T-cell activation indicate an active, functional biological response to an administered antigen, but they do not guarantee absolute protection against clinical infection, especially in the presence of overwhelming viral challenge, mucosal portal entry, or evolving pathogen variants (7, 8, 10). Furthermore, immune protection is often multifaceted; an individual with waning circulating antibodies may maintain robust anamnestic cellular memory sufficient to prevent severe hospitalization while remaining susceptible to mild infection (13, 23). Therefore, PLIM does not claim to deliver absolute biological certainty. Instead, it provides health systems with an intermediate biological probability metric that significantly refines risk estimation beyond administrative headcounts alone.A critical consideration for the implementation of PLIM across resource-constrained health systems is financial sustainability and cost efficiency. Rather than duplicating parallel structures or introducing unsustainable overheads, PLIM’s economic viability is anchored in two structural efficiencies: capital minimization at the point of care and the preemptive avoidance of reactive outbreak control. By relying on ambiently air-dried Dried Blood Spot (DBS) cards collected at routine immunization touchpoints, the architecture eliminates the prohibitive capital and maintenance costs associated with uninterrupted reverse cold-chain networks required for conventional venous serum transport, reducing field collection and logistics expenditures by up to 70% (11, 12). At the reference hub tier, high-throughput quantitative ELISA platforms utilize standardized commercial assays with marginal reagent costs estimated between $3.00 and $7.00 USD per specimen, while resource-intensive cellular assays are strictly restricted to a 10% research subsample (13, 14). From an economic framework perspective, these modest marginal surveillance costs must be evaluated against the staggering societal and budgetary burdens of reactive outbreak containment. Large-scale reactive campaigns for vaccine-preventable resurgences—such as measles outbreaks—routinely incur emergency operational costs exceeding tens of millions of dollars, compound secondary mortality, and erode public health trust. By delivering prospective pharmacodynamic intelligence that identifies localized waning immunity before community transmission triggers an epidemic, PLIM operates as a high-value, cost-averting surveillance layer that aligns proactive biological quality assurance with sustainable health-system financing (8, 11).
full_text_sections.conclusion: ConclusionThe ultimate promise of vaccination lies not in the delivery of a vial, but in the generation of sustained immunity. In Sub-Saharan Africa, where diverse immunologic, genetic, and environmental factors converge at the ‘last mile’, this promise is frequently disrupted by a persistent and often invisible vaccine performance gap. We have presented Population-Level Immunologic Monitoring (PLIM) as a strategic architecture to help map this gap. By embedding routine, sentinel immunologic verification into national immunization programs, PLIM transforms Public Health Pharmacology from a theoretical discipline into an operational tool. It empowers health ministries to detect waning immunity trends early, optimize booster strategies dynamically, and ensure that the mandate of ‘health for all’ translates into ‘protection for all’. As the continent moves toward the next generation of vaccines and local manufacturing autonomy, our metrics for success must evolve. While absolute biological certainty remains elusive due to the inherently probabilistic nature of immune protection and context-dependent correlates of immunity, we can no longer afford to ask only, ‘How many were reached?’ We must implement the systems required to evaluate, with high epidemiological and biological probability, ‘How many are protected?’ PLIM provides the structured, complementary framework to answer that question.
full_text_sections.other: BackgroundVaccination remains one of the most effective tools in combating infectious diseases globally, yet significant challenges persist in translating clinical availability into sustained field effectiveness within Sub-Saharan Africa. Despite widespread immunization initiatives, numerous endemically burdened regions continue to experience outbreaks and waning protection. This persistence suggests potential systemic gaps in vaccine performance that go beyond simple issues of access or coverage.The discrepancy between trial efficacy and real-world impact is often profound. For instance, the Bacille Calmette–Guérin (BCG) vaccine demonstrates efficacy ranging from 60 to 80% in temperate climates but drops to near zero in equatorial settings, a variation likely driven by environmental mycobacterial interference and parasitic co-infections (1, 2). Similarly, long-term follow-up of the RTS, S/AS01 malaria vaccine reveals that effectiveness is not static; it decreases in high-transmission settings and wanes significantly depending on the demographic and genetic profile of the population (3, 4). Compounding these genetic and environmental vectors are severe nutritional deficiencies, which actively function as biological modifiers of host immunity in resource-limited settings. Chronic micronutrient deficiencies, particularly zinc and vitamin A shortages, mechanically impair lymphoid tissue architecture, disrupt B-cell affinity maturation, and diminish mucosal IgA production, thereby significantly dampening the expected biological yield of routine oral and systemic vaccines (5, 6). The COVID-19 rollout further illustrated this disconnect, where ‘effectiveness’ was often assumed based on foreign trial data rather than verified against local variants and host immune profiles (7, 8). Collectively, these examples highlight a ‘vaccine performance gap’: the divergence between the theoretical biological potency of a vaccine and its actual immunological yield in the ‘last mile’ of African health systems.To address this complex interplay of host genomic diversity, nutritional deficiencies, and environmental co-exposures, public health systems require an explicit epistemological framework. While PHP interfaces with epidemiology, immunology, clinical pharmacology, and implementation science, it is not merely an intersection; it addresses an unmonitored structural blind spot that none of these parent disciplines examine individually. Epidemiology tracks disease transmission patterns across populations but largely treats the pharmacological agent as a fixed, uniform input. Implementation Science focuses on delivery systems, cold chain logistics, and dose administration (“last-mile access”) under the operational assumption that an intact vial delivered equates to biological protection. Clinical Pharmacology characterizes pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic mechanisms, but traditionally restricts its inquiry to controlled, homogenous, and often non-representative clinical trial cohorts. We propose that these systemic biological challenges fall under the domain of Public Health Pharmacology (PHP). Defined in our foundational work as “the discipline that studies the population-level behavior, effectiveness, safety, distribution, and strategic deployment of pharmacological agents within public health systems” (9). PHP uniquely investigates population-level pharmacodynamics. It evaluates how real-world population heterogeneity—including widespread endemic parasitic co-infections, endemic micronutrient malnutrition, regional genetic diversity, and climate-driven physiological stress—modifies the biological mechanism, immunogenic yield, and duration of protection of pharmacological agents deployed at public health scale. papers.title_original: Public Health Pharmacology: a framework for population-level immunologic monitoring (PLIM) to optimize vaccine performance in Africa

analysis.research_question_and_background: This paper addresses the need for a systematic approach to bridge the gap between vaccine coverage and clinical outcomes in public health, proposing a framework for Population-Level Immunologic Monitoring (PLIM) to optimize vaccine performance in Africa.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study describes a prospective "Pathfinder Pilot" validation roadmap in Rwanda, employing a stratified purposive sampling design across three ecological and health-system strata: high-density urban settings, rural endemic regions, and agro-climatic thermal stress zones. Sampling includes infants presenting for routine Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) schedules and pregnant women during antenatal care visits.
analysis.methods: Sampling operates on a dual cadence, combining rapid, rolling cross-sectional bi-annual audits and prospective longitudinal cohort tracking. Immunologic data points are integrated directly into national health information systems, such as the DHIS2 Tracker, and environmental metrics are incorporated to investigate biological interactions.
analysis.main_results: The paper outlines a conceptual framework for PLIM, emphasizing its role in systematically bridging the gap between vaccine coverage and clinical outcomes. It highlights the integration of immunologic data into health systems and the use of sentinel surveillance models.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret PLIM as a novel systems-design framework that provides a missing biological baseline to explain vaccine success or failure. They argue that it functions as an active, prospective pharmacodynamic audit rather than a retrospective evaluation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: PLIM can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and risk assessment by offering a structured platform to investigate biological interactions affecting vaccine response. It enables health systems to distinguish between programmatic and biological failures, enhancing targeted interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a conceptual framework and a prospective "Pathfinder Pilot" validation roadmap in Rwanda, which may not be generalizable to other regions. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a proposed design rather than empirical results.

analysis.summary_en: This paper introduces a novel conceptual framework for Population-Level Immunologic Monitoring (PLIM) as a core tool in Public Health Pharmacology (PHP) to bridge the gap between vaccine coverage and clinical outcomes in Africa. The study outlines a prospective "Pathfinder Pilot" validation roadmap in Rwanda, employing a stratified purposive sampling design across three ecological and health-system strata. It emphasizes the integration of immunologic data into national health information systems and the use of sentinel surveillance models to adapt strategies from HIV and malaria monitoring. The framework aims to provide a biological baseline for understanding vaccine performance, enabling health systems to differentiate between programmatic and biological failures. While the study presents a conceptual design, it does not include empirical results, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate. The implications of PLIM include improving surveillance, diagnosis, and risk assessment by incorporating environmental metrics and real-time data into health systems.

papers.title: Identification of Mpox Skin Lesion Images Based on Deep Learning Classification Models
papers.abstract: Mpox (formerly known as monkeypox) is a rare zoonotic disease that can cause skin lesions and has the potential for global spread. With the deepening integration of computer science and medicine, intelligent disease detection models based on deep learning and neural networks have become important auxiliary tools for enhancing clinical diagnosis and treatment. This study conducted a comparative analysis of the performance of mainstream deep learning classification models,VGG19, ResNet50, DenseNet201, GoogLeNet, and ConvNeXt_B,in the task of mpox skin image recognition. For the binary classification task, images were categorized into a “Mpox” class and an “Others” class, where the latter includes chickenpox and measles cases, given that their initial rash and pustule presentations closely resemble those of mpox. Beyond quantitative performance evaluation, this study further employed GradCAM++ to generate class activation heatmaps, providing visual interpretability of model decision-making. The resulting heatmaps offer critical clinical diagnostic value by highlighting key lesion regions, thereby enhancing model transparency and supporting clinicians in validating predictions. The experimental results indicate that under identical model parameters and learning rates, the ResNet50 model achieved higher classification accuracy and inference speed, demonstrating its application potential for accurate diagnosis in mpox and other disease image recognition tasks.
papers.journal: Frontiers in artificial intelligence and applications

papers.title_zh: 基于深度学习分类模型的痘痘皮损图像识别
papers.source_body_en: Mpox (formerly known as monkeypox) is a rare zoonotic disease that can cause skin lesions and has the potential for global spread. With the deepening integration of computer science and medicine, intelligent disease detection models based on deep learning and neural networks have become important auxiliary tools for enhancing clinical diagnosis and treatment. This study conducted a comparative analysis of the performance of mainstream deep learning classification models,VGG19, ResNet50, DenseNet201, GoogLeNet, and ConvNeXt_B,in the task of mpox skin image recognition. For the binary classification task, images were categorized into a “Mpox” class and an “Others” class, where the latter includes chickenpox and measles cases, given that their initial rash and pustule presentations closely resemble those of mpox. Beyond quantitative performance evaluation, this study further employed GradCAM++ to generate class activation heatmaps, providing visual interpretability of model decision-making. The resulting heatmaps offer critical clinical diagnostic value by highlighting key lesion regions, thereby enhancing model transparency and supporting clinicians in validating predictions. The experimental results indicate that under identical model parameters and learning rates, the ResNet50 model achieved higher classification accuracy and inference speed, demonstrating its application potential for accurate diagnosis in mpox and other disease image recognition tasks.

papers.title: Does a prenatal consultation dedicated to fathers’ health widen men’s access to prevention and care?
papers.abstract: Prenatal care provides expectant mothers with regular healthcare access, yet no equivalent preventative framework exists for expectant fathers. The PARTAGE project evaluated a dedicated prenatal consultation for future fathers aimed at health preservation and improvement. We describe the clinical outcomes of this consultation and identify factors associated with these outcomes. PARTAGE was a monocentric interventional study without control arm launched in a large public maternity ward in a northeastern suburb of Paris, an area where immigration prevails. Eligible pregnant women were offered to give their partner contact details. Among 2516 eligible future fathers who were successfully contacted, 1333 were included; fourteen others sought the consultation directly. A physician or a midwife held a medical interview, prescribed immediate biological tests, administered vaccination catch-up, and offered healthcare and social referral depending on participants' needs. Paternal prenatal consultations resulted in prevention, diagnosis and linkage into care: 37% of participants had never been tested for HIV; 96% had not been tested during or immediately prior to the current pregnancy, of whom only 1% refused HIV screening; 72% were out-of-date for pertussis or measles vaccinations, of whom 60% received an on-site catch-up. In addition, 18% had at least one pathology diagnosed or brought back into care; 17% were referred to healthcare professionals and 11% to social workers. In multivariate analysis, being born in Sub Saharan Africa rather than in France and having no health insurance coverage rather than a complete one were associated with a medical diagnosis (OR 2.67 [1.80-3.98] and OR 2.58 [1.63-4.09], respectively) and with a referral to a healthcare professional (OR 2.67 [1.80-3.98] and OR 3.63 [2.27-5.80], respectively). PARTAGE led to HIV screening and vaccinations catch-up across the whole study population. It also enabled the diagnosis of undetected illnesses and to the resumption of care for pathologies that had already been diagnosed but were previously lost to follow-up, especially in the most socially disadvantaged future fathers. Addressing men’s health during their partner’s pregnancy may help reduce gender and social inequalities in health. NCT05085717; Registry: ClinicalTrials.gov, US National Library of Medicine https://classic.clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT05085717 (retrospectively registered). Registration date: 20 October 2021. Protocol is available as additional file 1.

analysis.methods: The study involved a medical interview, prescribed biological tests, vaccinations, and referrals to healthcare and social services based on participants' needs.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study found that paternal prenatal consultations led to significant prevention, diagnosis, and linkage into care, particularly for socially disadvantaged men. It also enabled the diagnosis of undetected illnesses and to the resumption of care for pathologies that had already been diagnosed but were previously lost to follow-up, especially in the most socially disadvantaged future fathers. Addressing men’s health during their partner’s pregnancy may help reduce gender and social inequalities in health. Protocol is available as additional file 1.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估针对准父亲的专门产前咨询,以改善健康结果并解决健康差异。对母亲的产前护理很完善,但对父亲却没有同等的框架。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: PARAGE 项目是在巴黎东北郊的一个大型公共产房进行的一项单中心介入研究,重点关注了 1333 名被联系的未来父亲以及 14 名直接寻求咨询的人。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究涉及医学访谈、规定的生物测试、疫苗接种 以及根据参与者的需求转介至医疗保健和社会服务。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在参与者中,37% 的人从未接受过 HIV 检测,96% 的人在当前怀孕期间或之前没有接受过检测,72% 的人未接受过百日咳或 麻疹 麻疹 疫苗接种 的检测,60% 的人接受了补充 疫苗接种。此外,18% 的人患有未确诊的病症,17% 的人被转介给医疗保健专业人员,11% 的人被转介给社会工作者。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,父亲的产前咨询可以起到显着的预防作用,并与护理挂钩,特别是对于社会弱势男性。出生在撒哈拉以南非洲地区或没有健康保险与较高的医疗 诊断 率和转诊至医疗保健专业人员有关。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,解决男性伴侣怀孕期间的健康问题有助于减少健康方面的性别和社会不平等,特别是在移民较多的地区。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其单中心设计和缺乏对照组而受到限制,这可能会影响普遍性。结果基于观察数据,可能会受到混杂因素的影响。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study highlights the global burden of measles and pertussis, emphasizing the need to build more resilient and sustainable vaccination programs to address ongoing challenges in disease prevention.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of existing literature and data on measles and pertussis trends, focusing on global vaccination programs and their effectiveness in reducing disease incidence.
analysis.methods: The methods involve analyzing trends in measles and pertussis cases from global studies and reports, including data from the GBD 2023 Pertussis Collaborators and GBD 2023 Measles Collaborators, as well as references to the World Health Organization and other relevant organizations.
analysis.main_results: The results indicate that measles and pertussis remain significant public health challenges, with recent data showing that vaccination programs have been effective in reducing disease burden but are vulnerable to disruptions, underscoring the need for resilience.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as a call to action for strengthening global vaccination programs, noting that while progress has been made, the threat of disease resurgence remains, and this study adds to the growing body of evidence supporting the need for resilient systems.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of more resilient and sustainable vaccination programs, which are critical for maintaining disease control and preventing outbreaks in vulnerable populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on existing literature and data, which may have limitations in terms of completeness and timeliness, but the evidence is strong due to its reliance on comprehensive global datasets and expert analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study underscores the importance of building resilient and sustainable vaccination programs in light of the ongoing global burden of measles and pertussis. By analyzing trends in disease incidence and the effectiveness of current vaccination strategies, the authors highlight the need for improved preparedness and adaptability in public health systems. The findings emphasize that while vaccination has significantly reduced disease prevalence, disruptions and gaps in coverage pose a continued risk. The study draws on data from the GBD 2023 Pertussis and Measles Collaborators, as well as the World Health Organization, to support its conclusions. The implications of the study are significant for global health policy, advocating for stronger surveillance, resource allocation, and program design to ensure long-term success. However, the reliance on existing data may limit the depth of insights, and the evidence is considered strong due to its broad scope and integration of multiple sources.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究强调了 麻疹 和百日咳的全球负担,强调需要建立更具弹性和可持续的 麻疹 计划,以应对疾病预防方面持续存在的挑战。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究回顾了有关 麻疹 和百日咳趋势的现有文献和数据,重点关注全球 麻疹 计划及其在减少疾病 发病率 方面的有效性。
elements_zh.methods: 这些方法涉及分析来自全球研究和报告的 麻疹 和百日咳病例的趋势,包括来自 GBD 2023 百日咳合作者和 GBD 2023 麻疹 合作者的数据,以及对世界卫生组织和其他相关组织的参考。

papers.title: Prediction Uncertainty Controlled Computer Model Calibration
papers.abstract: Computer-model calibration is usually undertaken in service of prediction, yet neither Bayesian Kennedy-O'Hagan (KOH) calibration nor amortized simulation-based inference is built to control the predictive error of the calibrated simulator. When parameters are weakly identified or the data-model discrepancy is misspecified, the simulator-output bands induced by a nominal posterior level can be far from nominal. We propose a two-layer framework that targets predictive miscoverage directly. First, a conditional flow-matching model learns an amortized posterior for the calibration parameters, trained on simulator outputs perturbed with Gaussian-process discrepancies of varying structure. Second, conformal risk control arranges posterior draws for the target observation into nested candidate sets and selects the smallest one whose fixed-rank pointwise bands attain a prescribed time-averaged miscoverage on a synthetic calibration sample. Under exchangeability of calibration and target observations, the bands control expected miscoverage in finite samples. In a synthetic benchmark, the proposed bands are roughly 20% the width of KOH-MCMC bands with miscoverage near the 10% target. In calibrating an age-structured SEIR model to the 2010 Malawi measles outbreak, they are again sharper and near-nominal, and the weeks they fail to cover coincide with the asymmetric epidemic decline, exposing structural inadequacy of the mechanistic model.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the limitations of existing calibration methods for computer models by proposing a new framework that directly controls predictive miscoverage. The background highlights that neither Bayesian Kennedy-O'Hagan (KOH) calibration nor amortized simulation-based inference adequately manages predictive error when parameters are weakly identified or data-model discrepancy is misspecified.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a synthetic benchmark and the calibration of an age-structured SEIR model to the 2010 Malawi measles outbreak. It focused on evaluating the performance of the proposed framework in these specific contexts.
analysis.methods: The methods included a two-layer framework: first, a conditional flow-matching model was used to learn an amortized posterior for calibration parameters, trained on simulator outputs with Gaussian-process discrepancies. Second, conformal risk control was applied to arrange posterior draws into nested candidate sets, selecting the smallest set that achieves a prescribed time-averaged miscoverage.
analysis.main_results: In the synthetic benchmark, the proposed bands were approximately 20% narrower than KOH-MCMC bands, with miscoverage close to the 10% target. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret their findings as demonstrating that their framework effectively controls predictive miscoverage in finite samples under exchangeability assumptions. The novelty lies in directly targeting predictive miscoverage through a two-layer approach, offering improved precision over existing methods.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for improving the accuracy of predictive models used in epidemiological studies, particularly for diseases like measles where precise forecasting is critical for public health interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to synthetic benchmarks and a single real-world measles outbreak, which may affect generalizability. The evidence is strong, as the framework was validated on both simulated and empirical data, showing consistent performance.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a two-layer framework for computer-model calibration aimed at directly controlling predictive miscoverage. The authors highlight that existing methods, such as Bayesian Kennedy-O'Hagan (KOH) calibration and amortized simulation-based inference, are inadequate when parameters are weakly identified or data-model discrepancy is misspecified. The framework combines a conditional flow-matching model with conformal risk control to produce narrower predictive bands with near-target miscoverage. When applied to a synthetic benchmark and the 2010 Malawi measles outbreak, the method demonstrated improved precision, though it failed to cover certain weeks during the asymmetric decline of the epidemic, indicating potential structural limitations in the mechanistic model. The study's results suggest that the framework could enhance the accuracy of predictive models in epidemiology, particularly for measles, with strong evidence from both simulated and empirical data. However, the limited scope to a single outbreak may restrict generalizability.

papers.abstract_zh: 计算机模型校准通常用于预测,但贝叶斯肯尼迪-奥哈根 (KOH) 校准和基于摊销模拟的推理都不是为了控制校准模拟器的预测误差而构建的。当参数识别不力或数据模型差异指定错误时,由标称后验水平引起的模拟器输出带可能远离标称值。我们提出了一个直接针对预测性错误覆盖的两层框架。首先,条件流匹配模型学习校准参数的摊销后验,并在受到不同结构的高斯过程差异扰动的模拟器输出上进行训练。其次,保形风险控制将目标观察的后验抽签安排到嵌套候选集中,并选择其固定秩逐点带在合成校准样本上达到规定的时间平均错误覆盖率的最小候选集。在校准和目标观测的可互换性下,这些带控制了有限样本中的预期错误覆盖。在综合基准中,建议的频带宽度约为 KOH-MCMC 频带宽度的 20%,误覆盖率接近 10% 的目标。在根据 2010 年马拉维 麻疹 暴发 校准年龄结构 SEIR 模型时,它们再次变得更加尖锐且接近名义值,并且它们未能涵盖的周数与不对称的流行病下降一致,暴露了机械模型的结构性不足。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过提出一个直接控制预测错误覆盖的新框架来解决计算机模型现有校准方法的局限性。背景强调,当参数识别较弱或数据模型差异指定错误时,贝叶斯肯尼迪-奥哈根 (KOH) 校准和基于摊销的模拟推理都无法充分管理预测误差。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及综合基准以及针对 2010 年马拉维 麻疹 暴发 的年龄结构 SEIR 模型的校准。它的重点是评估所提议的框架在这​​些特定背景下的性能。
analysis_zh.methods: 这些方法包括一个两层框架:首先,使用条件流匹配模型来学习校准参数的摊销后验,并在具有高斯过程差异的模拟器输出上进行训练。其次,应用保形风险控制将后验抽签安排到嵌套的候选集中,选择实现规定的时间平均错误覆盖的最小集。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在综合基准中,建议的频带比 KOH-MCMC 频带窄约 20%,误覆盖率接近 10% 的目标。当应用于 2010 年马拉维 麻疹 麻疹 暴发 时,这些区间更加尖锐且接近名义值,尽管它们未能覆盖非对称流行病下降期间的某些周。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为证明他们的框架在可交换性假设下有效控制了有限样本中的预测错误覆盖。新颖之处在于通过两层方法直接针对预测性错误覆盖,提供比现有方法更高的精度。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对于提高流行病学研究中使用的预测模型的准确性具有重要意义,特别是对于 麻疹 等疾病,精确的预测对于公共卫生干预措施至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于综合基准和单个现实世界的 麻疹 暴发,这可能会影响普遍性。证据是强有力的,因为该框架在模拟和经验数据上都得到了验证,显示出一致的性能。

papers.full_text: Linear enamel hypoplasia (LEH) is a failure or aberration of enamel to form correctly, resulting in bands of decreased enamel on the tooth surface. Many reasons, including genetics, malnutrition, and childhood diseases, can cause LEH, which solely affects the neonatal line. LEH is a kind of environmental hypoplasia with many symmetrical and ring-like abnormalities. Amelogenesis is a one-time procedure, and any abnormality might result in permanent enamel abnormalities. Enamel, unlike other human tissues, cannot be restored. The consequences of enamel hypoplasia vary based on illness severity, etiological agent interaction, and patient age upon presentation. The article provides information on the etiology, epidemiology, clinical features, and differential diagnosis of LEH. DiscussionDefinitionLEH refers to a visible alteration of the tooth crown surface, which may be observed under a microscope or with the naked eye. It appears as bands of different widths and depths that perpendicularly run around the tooth crown to its long axis [1].EtiologyEnamel hypoplasia is primarily attributed to childhood illnesses and accidents. Hence, enamel hypoplasia can be regarded as a comprehensive marker of malnutrition and disease in elderly people [1]. The process of dental calcification is not independent but rather closely connected to the tooth's eruption and the development of the surrounding tissues [2].The cause of enamel hypoplasia is linked to substances that disrupt the functioning of ameloblasts, which are cells responsible for generating enamel. This interference can lead to a decrease or complete halt in their activity. The deficiencies that can occur include protein deficiencies (such as amelogenin, enamelin, and tuftelin), vitamin deficiencies (A, C, K, and D), deficiencies of calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, or fluorine, diseases of the pituitary such as dwarfism, parathyroid disorders such as hypoparathyroidism, hypothyroidism, and Addison's disease. Bacterial infections such as tuberculosis and tetanus, viral infections such as rubella, measles, and herpes zoster, and spirochaetal infections such as syphilis disrupt the functioning of the ameloblasts [2].Dental enamel hypoplasia refers to regions of reduced thickness in the enamel layer. These regions form when there is a disruption in the process of ameloblast deposition on the growing crowns of permanent and primary teeth. The production of enamel matrix is hindered due to increased levels of cortisol, which impede protein synthesis as a consequence of a stress episode. Numerous causes have been linked to their occurrence [3]. The distribution of abnormalities is very similar in terms of their position on the tooth crown; even though the chronology of enamel hypoplasia varies among teeth, the frequency of such LEH peaks near the crown's midway. The enamel prisms at this position on the crown are virtually perpendicular to the surface. This orientation may make it simpler to identify changes in rod lengths [3]. It was found that the rate of crown formation will rise at this period. The tooth was more vulnerable to interruption of enamel formation due to the rapid rate of enamel deposition during tooth development in these areas. Hypoplasia was characterized as circumferential bands, lines, or low pits with diminished enamel thickness [3].Enamel hypoplasia is when the enamel becomes thinner due to the complete or partial suppression of ameloblast function during the secretory phase of enamel production. It can be classified into pits, lines, and grooves. The latter two are specifically known as LEH [4].Methods of assessment of LEHThe various methods of assessment of LEH are presented in Table 1.Table 1Various methods to determine linear enamel hypoplasia (LEH).The table was modified and created with permission from the authors [3-11].AuthorYearMethodMethod of CalculationAdvantageDisadvantagesMassler M and Schour I [3]1941Chart methodAge at LEH formation 1⁄4 = - [1/velocity x distance of LEH from CEJ] + age at crown completionA significant number of bioarchaeologists use them. Minimal computation toolsCharts do not possess separate surveys for females and males.Ensor BE and Irish JD [4]1995Tooth hypoplastic area (THA) methodAcute hypoplasia or a one-stress event is given a value of 0.10. The crown disturbance percentage for chronic hypoplasia is calculated by dividing the defect's width by two-thirds of the estimated crown height. For example, if 70% of the crown is affected, the value assigned is 0.7%; if 50% of the crown surface is affected, it is 0.5%. The sum of these values is termed total hypoplastic area (THA).Canines are commonly selected for analysis as they tend to have higher levels of hypoplasia and are more usually retained.It is not possible to evaluate third molars. Assessing tooth loss caused by attrition is not possible. The majority of archaeological remains typically lack complete sets of teeth. S is the Standard Error of the Regression.Included central and lateral incisors and canines.Not included molars for estimating linear enamel hypoplasia (LEH).Reid DJ and Dean MC [6]2006Reid and Dean's methodX= d/(l/l-m) x 10 "x" is the distance of the defect from the CEJ along a standardized 10 mm tooth (d), the observed distance of the start of the defect from the CEJ in mm is divided by the length of the tooth available (i.e., length of the surface profile) in mm (l), which itself is divided by the percentage of the tooth that is missing (1-m) The crown is divided into deciles of crown height, and then the number of days required for each decile to develop is calculated.The time required for the creation of the Cusp is taken into account. The observed features extend beyond the usual width of a single perikymata for the specific third of the tooth's crown in which they appear.It relies on the depth of the enamel surface.The accumulation of calculus on the surface of the enamel might result in enduring positive residuals. The steep angle at which these growth planes of enamel occur in the upper part of the tooth causes a greater distance between the ridges, resulting in enamel hypoplasia defects that are less deep and less well characterized.Hasset [8]2012Micrometric methodPerikymata that are significantly deviated from a moving or local z-score by at least one standard deviation is amplified. It enables the unbiased identification and quantitative analysis of the sequence and length of defects. It also minimizes the chance of subjective judgment and enhances the precision and reproducibility of findings. Sensofar Plu Neox confocal microscope [11]2024Microscopic analysisThe vertical axis of each tooth crown (y-axis), from the CEJ to the incisal edge.Resolution of 1.6 μm.Linear enamel hypoplasia (LEH) measures are affected by the presence of depressions caused by pits, elevations, or fissures resulting from concretions or other materials attached to the enamel surface.LEH, a dental anomaly associated with nutritional or other stress factors, was initially discovered in a Neolithic mammal in Hungary [12].When the central region of the crown is impacted by hypoplasia, there is a noticeable alteration in the ratios of carbon and oxygen isotopes. This outcome is predictable since the development of LEH is connected to disruptions linked to the absorption of food, which is likely to be indicated by changes in the concentration of stable isotopes derived from the diet. LEH is caused by the physiological stress associated with the challenges encountered during the weaning stage [13].EpidemiologyThe prevalence of enamel hypoplasia was 12.8% [13]. The young individuals from Jabuticabeira II likely encountered frequent episodes of stress, potentially caused by infectious, diarrheal, and parasitic disorders. This stress was likely linked to introducing a "high-risk" diet, which may have included contaminated marine food in their supplementary and adult diets. LEH observed in adults indicates that these individuals have successfully overcome challenges experienced in early life. However, the presence of LEH in adolescents suggests a connection with an unidentified cause of death. In Jabuticabeira II, the individuals who managed to survive would have experienced frequent periods of illness (such as anemia, infections, and general stress), most likely caused by the high number of parasites in the environment and poor sanitation. Malnutrition, although possible, was probably not the leading cause of their health problems [14].A comprehensive analysis was conducted on a combined total of 25 Italian cemetery remains and 139 migrants to assess the occurrence and intensity of LEH. This study has demonstrated that migrants have a higher frequency and greater severity of stress markers compared to the Italian group. Furthermore, these brain lesions are physical manifestations of the physiological disturbances they have endured. In reaction to stressors that affect the body's systems throughout growth, skeletal remains can show bone lesions, including cortical osteitis (CO), periosteal hyperostosis (PH), and LEH. The migrants' early life was characterized by poor living conditions and poverty, indirectly caused by social and economic inequalities. These conditions led to preventable biological harm, such as malnutrition, dietary insufficiencies, and infections. These bone lesions are a clear manifestation of the structural violence resulting from these circumstances [15].LEH manifests as a dark-colored band that runs parallel to the incremental lines of enamel. This band is typically found between the neonatal line and the gingival margin in the incisors [15].The high frequency and severity of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) indicate a range of stressful events in a child's life [15]. The age range of faults and peaks in LEH production, as determined, was more remarkable for the maxillary teeth than for the mandibular teeth [15]. The prevalence of maxillary dentition was 27.6% for central incisors, whereas it was 35.4% for lateral incisors in mandibular dentition. The highest incidence of LEH defects was observed in young individuals (54.3%), followed by middle adults (50.0%), and the lowest frequency was recorded in old adults (40.0%) [15]. LEH of the deciduous maxillary incisors was observed in 73.1% of 104 Guatemalan children who were recuperating from their third stage of development [16]; 42.9% of the 150 youngsters undergoing treatment had second-degree malnutrition. The prevalence rates for these children from Guatemala are considerably higher compared to those reported for children from other regions of Guatemala. The correlation between an event that happened during the first month of life (linear hypoplasia) and the later occurrence of malnutrition (kwashiorkor and marasmus) may have epidemiological importance in identifying specific groups of children who would greatly benefit from food supplementation programs [16].Differential diagnosisThe differential diagnosis for LEH includes MIH and Blaschko linear enamel defects. The teeth affected by MIH exhibit clearly defined boundaries of hypomineralized enamel, distinct from the opaque areas seen in fluorosis [17]. They were spread out over a wide area. Fluorosed enamel is more resistant to tooth decay than enamel afflicted by caries-prone MIH [18].MIH is a distinct type of dental enamel defect (DDE) caused by systemic sickness and is defined by hypomineralization. This hypomineralization is observed as translucency in the enamel. Systemic factors often result in environmental enamel hypoplasia/hypomineralization, most typically observed in the first permanent molars and incisors. Enamel hypoplasia primarily affects the teeth that develop during the first year after birth, as indicated by clinical research. The incisors and primary permanent molars are the teeth that are most commonly affected. Therefore, this disease is referred to as MIH. When observed in a clinical setting, these abnormalities with less mineralization often deteriorate due to the pressure exerted during chewing. They appear as areas with a combination of underdevelopment and reduced mineral content. The premolars and the second and third molars are rarely impacted since their development commences at age three or later [18]. The vertical grooves on the teeth, known as Blaschko linear enamel defects, indicate the migration and growth of epidermal cells during embryonic development. These grooves are highly characteristic of focal dermal hypoplasia (FDH) [19].TreatmentRemineralizing agent casein phosphopeptide-amorphous calcium phosphate (CPP-ACP) (Recaldent, GC Tooth Mousse, GC Corporation, Sharjah, United Arab Emirates) aids in the remineralization of hypoplastic areas of enamel in LEH. Composite restoration helps recontour the lost surface of the enamel defect caused by LEH [20]. ConclusionsLEH must not be overlooked during a dental examination. It can cause problems with esthetics, tooth sensitivity, malocclusion, and an increased risk of dental caries. In its mildest form, LEH is often misdiagnosed as decay, as most teeth are prone to decay. Early recognition of LEH is critical because it primarily concerns aesthetics. Dentists have the chance to prevent these abnormalities through anticipatory guidance. A precise diagnosis is required to differentiate other illnesses and develop a conservative treatment approach if LEH is already present. Early diagnosis, treatment planning, and prognosis of LEH are crucial for preventing its complications from restoring esthetics and increasing masticatory efficiency. IntroductionLinear enamel hypoplasia (LEH) is identified in populations due to amelogenesis disruption as a sign of stress. Stress in the form of trauma, diet, viral illnesses, and environmental variations can alter enamel matrix production. Stresses in any form leave persistent physical traces on the teeth. Molar incisor hypomineralization (MIH) is a type of enamel defect that is qualitative and caused by decreased mineral density. In contrast, enamel hypoplasia is a quantitative enamel defect resulting from decreased enamel matrix secretion. However, in the most severe cases of MIH, the hypomineralized enamel might fracture, resulting in tissue thickness loss following tooth eruption. Enamel hypoplasia is characterized by a loss in enamel thickness that occurs before tooth eruption and, if associated with a systemic insult, affects all teeth growing at the time. At the transition to normal enamel, hypoplastic enamel lesions have regular margins but tend to fracture under occlusal forces, which are unevenly rough and appear in chalky-white or brownish-discolored areas [1]. Enamel hypoplasia occurs when enamel development is disrupted. The teeth most typically implicated are the central incisors, lateral incisors, canines, and molars; enamel production occurs within the first year following birth [2]. Her past medical history was non-contributory. She had no history of any drug intake for fever or illness. A general examination revealed her vitals were stable.
